A PC-relative mode branch instruction is stored in memory at address $620_{10}$ The size of the instruction is $2$ bytes. The branch is made to location $530_{10}$ and the address field in the instruction is $16$ bits long.

The value of displacement (in decimal) in the instruction is ____________

question.text:
A two-way set-associative cache has a line size of $16$ bytes and a total capacity of $8$ KB . The main memory is $64$ MB and byte-addressable. What is the format of a main memory address (Tag, Set Index, Block Offset)?

  1. $13$ bits Tag, $9$ bits Set, $4$ bits Offset
     
  2. $14$ bits Tag, $8$ bits Set, $4$ bits Offset
     
  3. $13$ bits Tag, $8$ bits Set, $4$ bits Offset
     
  4. $14$ bits Tag, $9$ bits Set, $4$ bits Offset
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A computer system has a main memory of $32$ K $16$-bit words and a cache of $4$ K words, organised into four-word lines with $64$ words per line. The cache is initially empty. A processor fetches words from memory locations $0,1,2, \ldots$, $4351$ in order, and then repeats this sequence $9$ more times. The cache is $10$ times faster than main memory. Assume an LRU block replacement policy.

What is the approximate performance improvement due to the cache?

  1.  $4 x$
     
  2. $6 x$
     
  3. $7 x$
     
  4. $10 x$
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
Consider a processor that includes a base with an indexing addressing mode. Suppose an instruction is encountered that employs this addressing mode and specifies a displacement of $1970$, in decimal. Currently the base and index registers contain the decimal numbers $48022$ and $8$, respectively.

The address of the operand (in decimal) is ____________.

question.text:
A program iterates over a one-dimensional array of $1024$ integers stored in memory. Each integer occupies $4$ bytes. The system has a direct-mapped L1 cache with the following characteristics:

  • Cache size $=256$ bytes
     
  • Block size $=16$ bytes
     
  • Cache miss penalty $=50 \mathrm{~ns}$
     
  • Cache hit time $=2 \mathrm{~ns}$

Consider the following program:

For(i=0 to length(array)-1 )
{

        Print(array[i])

}

What is the affective memory access time of the cache approximately (in $\mu \mathrm{s}$ ) for this loop?

  1. $14.5$
     
  2. $19.37$
     
  3. $0.0145$
     
  4. $15$
question.subject: CO & Architecture
